The 880 was the model designation for the hollow, saber ground version of the venerable Schrade 4 inch stockman pattern knife. It was made from 1950 to 1975, and these two knives "bookend" that time period.

The Knife on the right is a very early "Schrade Walden" stamped knife with the mark side of it's main blade polished and etched with the "Kon-Kav" branding (Schrade's trade name for hollow grinds at the time). The pile side, and the secondary blades are all glaze finished. The scales are dyed and jigged bone, which at the time (early 1950's) was becoming increasingly rare and hard to find, leading most companies to start working with synthetic materials about that time.

The knife on the left represents the tail end of 880 production. The blades are all glazed, and no etch is present. The "Schrade, NY, USA, 880" stamping dates the knife after 1973, as in the middle of that year the company changed it's name from Schrade Walden to Imperial Schrade and moved the factory from Walden to Ellenville, NY (and changed the stampings to reflect it). The handles are dyed Delrin, a type of Acetal plastic that saw widespread use in the cutlery industry and became a signature material at the Schrade companies.
